A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProAPO work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison; retained material can be matched across appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on thirteen datasets, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and adapter/backbone transfer results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, parameter and prompt-library sensitivity results, and computation-cost measurements.

M1.justification: Equation (5) changes the stated fitness term from expected negative log similarity to expected log similarity, while Equation (6) still adds this term to accuracy for maximization. This corrects the specified confidence preference. The progressive search, operators, and sampling algorithms remain unchanged; an implementation change or rerun is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same thirteen classification datasets and domains. The new comparisons use eleven- and eight-dataset subsets already represented in v1; the new sensitivity studies also reuse existing tasks.

E2.justification: v4 Appendix F adds evaluated comparisons with TPT, DiffTPT, PromptAlign, Self-TPT-v, UPT, CoCoOp, MaPLe, ALIGN, PromptSRC, and AWT variants in Table 9, plus iCM in Table 10. This substantially broadens comparator coverage beyond v1, including methods previously only cited.

E3.justification: Existing protocols and default settings are retained. Added experiments compare textual and adapter-equipped configurations, contrast one-shot ProAPO with validation-set-supervised iCM, and sweep the score weight and prompt-library sizes. These introduce additional evaluation settings without establishing revisions to the existing experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's operator, sampling, score-component, and shot-count analyses, v4 adds score-weight sensitivity (Table 16), query-prompt and generated-description budget studies (Figures 10–11), and computation-cost profiling (Table 14). These substantially extend examination of sensitivity, limited prompt resources, and efficiency.

E5.justification: Both versions specify averaging over four seeds, identified as 1, 2, 3, and 42 in Appendix D.1. Existing variability reporting is retained, and v4 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or statistical significance test.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and appendix values are retained, while new comparisons and analyses substantially expand reported results. Examples include Table 9 averages of 75.2 for ProAPO with APE and 75.1 for AWT-Adapter, and Table 16 accuracies of 62.3, 65.0, and 63.1 at score weights 0, 1000, and 100000. These are added results, not gains over matched v1 measurements.

T1.justification: Equation (5) removes the minus sign in the definition of H. Under the retained maximization objective, this is a substantive mathematical correction rather than equivalent notation. Other mathematical definitions remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: progressive prompt optimization with one-shot supervision, reduced costs and overfitting, strong thirteen-dataset results, and adapter/backbone transfer. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 newly interprets excessive score weight as causing training-set bias, discusses effectiveness with small prompt libraries, and argues that ProAPO and AWT are complementary. The high-shot performance and limited-search-space limitations already discussed in v1 Appendix G.1 are retained rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: v4 Table 14 adds runtime details: 60 minutes for library construction, 3 for sampling, 1.6 for template optimization, and 10.4 for description optimization. v1 reported overall optimization time without this breakdown. Hardware, implementation framework, existing hyperparameter disclosures, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references including DiffTPT, PromptSRC, PromptAlign, and UPT, and expands appendix positioning against test-time and vector-based prompt tuning and AWT. The main related-work narrative and original novelty rationale remain largely intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v4 inserts an appendix comparison section and several analysis subsections, updates the appendix outline and cross-references, and adds author contact information and an affiliation correction. The main argument is not extensively rewritten or reorganized.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 9, 10, 14, and 16 and Figures 10–11, with corresponding appendix reflow and renumbering. Existing method diagrams, principal result displays, and qualitative and transfer figures retain their content and overall design.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects the fitness-score sign and strengthens validation through broader comparisons, sensitivity studies, and clearer runtime accounting. These improve consistency and support for the existing method. However, the new AWT discussion claims a 6.1% gain although Table 9 shows 68.6% to 71.6%, a 3.0-percentage-point difference. The useful additions outweigh this localized reporting error, yielding a limited overall improvement.
